questions.problem: Which of the following diagrams shows all the $6$th roots of unity?
questions.worked_solution:
Geometrically, the $6$th roots of unity have the following properties:

- all of them lie on the unit circle centered in the origin,

- one of the roots is $1,$ corresponding to the point $(1,0)$ on the complex plane,

- the roots form a regular hexagon (regular $6$-sided polygon).

Therefore, the correct answer is the following:

questions.knowledge_point: Finding Roots of Unity With Certain Properties
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14043589/assets/91f4aac82208a2801652c9112f58518e1abc89ed4313601a60f7c183b7757f70.png)

Find the $10$th root of unity highlighted in the diagram above.
questions.worked_solution:
The $n$th roots of unity lie at the vertices of a regular $n$-gon inscribed inside the unit circle in the complex plane. One of the vertices of this regular $n$-gon must lie at the point $(1,0).$

First, we express the complex number $1$ in the form $r{e}^{\text{i}\theta }.$ Notice that $|1|=1$ and $\operatorname{arg}⁡(1)=0.$ Hence, 

$$
1={e}^{\text{i}(0+2k\pi )}={e}^{2k\pi \text{i}},
$$

where $k$ is an integer. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{10}={e}^{2k\pi \text{i}}\,⟹\,z=({e}^{2k\pi \text{i}})^{1/10}={e}^{k\pi \text{i}/5}.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the index $k$ of our root of unity, we enumerate the roots in the diagram counter-clockwise, starting with the root at $(1,0)$ corresponding to $k=0,$ as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14043589/assets/d0fc6866d4bb06ec6cbf20bb719faf722ec3c1efe3fba03e413f51dc1c827e71.png)

 

So, the required root corresponds to $k=8.$ Substituting this into the expression for roots, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}_{8}={e}^{(8)\pi \text{i}/5}={e}^{8\pi \text{i}/5}\end{aligned}
$$
